findings.summary: The authorised taper-floor fix (0.45 -> 0.85) landed and reached the render: IBM improved 3.522 -> 0.396 and every ribbon widened 1.89x. NBIS moved 33.846 -> 30.522 and sample-live-rgb.mjs still aborts at deltaE 33.123. Round 4's sub-pixel partial-coverage attribution is disproven. The 49px cross-section through NBIS's published sample point is a ~12px band peaking at red 93 against the model's 179, with zero pixels within 2 of the model; INTC at the same expected colour shows a 14px plateau at exactly 179. No DOM layer overlies the point (elementsFromPoint returns only the canvas over MAIN at rgb(1,5,4); panel-free pixel identical to shipped). The same NBIS arc does reach #aa231b, deltaE 3.44, 165px away. The opaque core is not at the published sample point on the outermost orbit; only the glow shoulders are.
findings.required_change: OWNER DECISION REQUIRED. The real mechanism is a registration error between the published data-trail-sample-x/y and where the opaque trail core renders on the outermost orbit — in the sample-point projection or the ribbon's angular sweep, not in trailRibbonHalfWidths. Bounded and specific, but new work not covered by the authorised bucket-A scope, and the triage rule has stopped §10 remediation. Do not change the verifier, its thresholds, or its sample points.

findings.bucket: A authorised, remediation failed; mechanism now disproven
findings.summary: The authorised handedness fix landed: sharp().flop() changes the generator's mark alpha by MAD 113.3 (MSFT) and 74.9 (CBRS) of 255, the two shipped 32x16 base thumbnails changed while untouched GOOG's is byte-identical at 0.000, and six KTX2 maps plus the manifest chirality strings changed. The panel-free correlation margin moved 0.018 (MSFT) and 0.021 (CBRS) — inside the 0.002-0.011 round-to-round drift of the five untouched worlds — and did NOT invert sign. Mirroring a mark must invert a correlation that reads that mark. The verifier's column-mean greyscale profile across the equatorial band is dominated by macro terrain, and the carved capital, which VIS-02 requires to share the terrain's lighting and be edge-eroded, contributes at or below that noise. The correlation cannot discriminate mark handedness, so it substantiates neither a pass nor a fail for any world, and round 4's 'genuinely mirrored marks' diagnosis is unsupported. Fourth consecutive round in which DEF-02 was attributed to texture generation and a regeneration moved the number by less than the noise.
findings.required_change: OWNER DECISION REQUIRED. Nothing inside §10's scope makes this criterion measurable. A verifier that samples the mark directly, rather than a terrain-dominated equatorial column profile, is new verifier work — which a review may not design and a remediation may not introduce. Do not weaken the assertion.

triage_rule.rule: After the NEXT review turn, remediation on §10 stops. Every open finding is sorted into bucket A (achievable inside §10 — one further remediation authorised), bucket B (real cause is §11 work; carry with the measurement attached and add to §11 acceptance, do not fix twice), or bucket C (criterion is unsatisfiable as specified — documented non-generalising owner exception with full measurement retained, the §1 pattern). The triage turn sets status=blocked, next_actor=devan and hands the classification to the owner; it does not self-authorise an exception.
triage_rule.why: Three of the last four sections (§1, §9, and §10 so far) closed by owner decision rather than a passing review. That indicates some criteria are calibrated above what is achievable, and the workflow has no way to discover it except by grinding until the owner intervenes. This converts an open-ended loop into one bounded decision.

section_1.acceptance_remediation_2_summary: Addressed both bounded Engineering Reliability findings from docs/phase10-reviews/2026-07-24-section-1-codex-acceptance-remediation.md. (1) Root-caused the 66-70ms long task via longtask attribution + resource-timing correlation to react-dom's client hydration chunk, then proved with a controlled same-route unauthenticated-baseline measurement that the task is caused entirely by the pre-existing (pre-Phase-10) root layout's DepthPullProvider + Next.js/React client runtime, not by the CSS 3D spike content itself (identical task duration with near-zero spike markup rendered). Because fixing this at the source requires editing src/app/layout.tsx in a way that changes / and /share (explicitly out of this remediation's scope), corrected the long-task budget from a whole-page absolute to an added-over-shared-shell-baseline differential, matching the methodology already used by the bundle and memory budgets in the same table; CSS 3D's added long-task time is ~0ms (median 0ms, range -1 to +13ms) vs R3F's ~119ms median, so CSS 3D now passes and the finding corroborates rather than weakens the existing decision. (2) Corrected the frame-stability script to capture exactly 60 raw rAF deltas and retain all of them; found the declared literal '<=16.7ms per sample' predicate is unachievable by any of the 20 retained runs (32-48/60 pass, universally, including both baselines) because 16.7ms sits on the exact 60Hz frame interval and ordinary timer jitter puts half of any smooth sequence fractionally above it; adopted the acceptance finding's explicitly allowed alternative (the >33.4ms dropped-frame predicate) as the graded criterion, under which every run on every route shows 0/60 dropped frames. Reran the full 5-repetition Moto G4 + CPU 4x + Slow 4G protocol for both routes plus new unauthenticated-baseline runs; CSS 3D now passes every declared threshold. See docs/phase10-spike-section-1/DECISION.md 'Long-task root cause and frame-stability predicate correction (acceptance remediation round 2)'.

single_provider_mode.reason: OpenAI quota exhausted until approximately 2026-08-03. Claude subscription upgraded to Max; OpenAI will not be upgraded.
single_provider_mode.activate_when: §10 is accepted. The remaining OpenAI credits are best spent finishing §10's two authorised bucket-A fixes under normal cross-model review; §11 onward runs Claude-only until quota returns.
single_provider_mode.suspended: Cross-model independence. Claude performs both roles. Recorded as a genuine reduction in review quality on every section accepted under it.
single_provider_mode.not_suspended: The relay invokes each turn as a separate process with no shared memory, so a Claude review still reads the spec, ledger, and artifacts cold. The loss is model diversity, not context isolation. Every other guarantee — acceptance ledger, live browser verification, privacy canaries, performance gates, state machine, lock — is unchanged.
compensating_controls: Executable ledger verifiers are required, not supporting; raw output retained.
No criterion graded from source reading alone; rendered behaviour needs a pixel, scene-graph, or DOM measurement.
Owner visual review before any acceptance — Devan is the independent check while the second model is unavailable.
Sections accepted under this mode set single_provider_mode:true in sections_history.
Implementation handoffs state what was measured, not argument; a reviewer must grade from artifacts alone.
must_wait_for_codex: Any change to the privacy boundary — /share rendering, the authenticated/public split, canary tests.
Any change to the financial math core — TWR, XIRR, drawdown, beta, Sharpe, volatility.
Weakening, redefining, or granting an exception to any gate.
single_provider_mode.operating: Run implementation turns with ./scripts/phase10-claude-lead.sh while state says next_actor: codex. The turn opens by recording that it acts under single-provider mode and which role it performs. Do NOT edit the state machine's role values — the record should show Claude covered a Codex turn, not that the workflow was rewritten around an outage.
